name: Refine and prioritize the product backlog
description: Break approved demand into sized, ordered work items with acceptance criteria, and agree the next increment with the business owner.

name: Design and build a software increment
description: Design, implement, and unit-test a work item to its acceptance criteria within the agreed architecture and standards.

name: Review and merge code
description: Peer-review a change for correctness, security, and standards before it is merged to the main line. Merge rights sit with reviewers, not authors, which is the segregation the change-control audit tests; review evidence stays on the pull request.

name: Run the build and deployment pipeline
description: Build, package, scan, and promote a change through environments automatically, with gates that stop a failing build.

name: Scan code and dependencies for security defects
description: Run static, dependency, and secret scanning on every change and remediate findings within the applicable service level.

name: Manage technical debt
description: Record, size, and prioritize technical debt, and reserve capacity in each increment to retire it. Debt items live in the same backlog as features so the trade-off is visible at prioritization, not discovered at incident time.

name: Manage application configuration and feature flags
description: Control configuration and feature-flag changes so behavior can be changed or reverted without a code release, with an audit trail.

name: Support a production application
description: Diagnose and fix application defects escalated from service management, and feed root causes back into the backlog.

name: Decommission an application
description: Retire an application: migrate or archive its data to the retention schedule, remove interfaces and access, and update the inventory.

name: Capture and apply cardholder payment
description: Accept a cardholder payment through any channel and apply it to the account on the correct effective date.

name: Assign delinquency treatment strategy
description: Segment delinquent accounts and assign the contact and treatment strategy. Runs nightly after delinquency bucketing; the strategy drives queue, channel, intensity, and hardship routing, and a wrong assignment is a conduct risk as much as a loss risk.

name: Execute outbound collections contact
description: Execute outbound contact attempts within contact-frequency and communication constraints. Contact windows, frequency caps, and channel consent come from FDCPA, Reg F, and TCPA; the process starts at queue release and ends when the disposition is recorded.

name: Negotiate and administer payment arrangement
description: Agree, document, and administer a payment arrangement or settlement. Covers promises to pay, long-term arrangements, and settlements; terms must fit the approved matrix, and the arrangement drives bucket movement and interest treatment downstream.

name: Execute charge-off
description: Execute charge-off on policy timing and record the accounting effect. Timing follows the charge-off policy aligned to regulatory guidance; the entry moves the balance to charged-off status and hands the account to recovery placement.

name: Furnish credit bureau data
description: Compile and furnish account data to the consumer reporting agencies. Monthly Metro 2 furnishing to the bureaus; accuracy is an FCRA obligation, and the file must reconcile to the system of record before transmission.

name: Handle credit reporting dispute
description: Investigate and respond to a consumer credit reporting dispute within the required period. Direct and bureau-routed disputes both land here; FCRA sets the investigation window, and the outcome must correct both the bureau file and the account when the consumer is right.

name: Issue debt validation notice
description: Generate and deliver the required validation notice within the prescribed period. The validation notice is a statutory precondition to continued collection on affected accounts; timing and content mistakes surface directly as regulatory findings.

name: Assess and land regulatory change
description: Detect a regulatory change, assess applicability and impact, and drive implementation. Starts at horizon scanning and ends when the change is implemented and evidenced in the affected processes; applicability calls are documented even when the answer is not applicable.

name: Execute compliance monitoring test
description: Execute a scheduled control test and record the result and any exceptions. Runs the monitoring schedule agreed with the compliance plan; exceptions become issues in remediation tracking with owners and dates rather than emails.

name: Screen for sanctions and watchlists
description: Screen parties and transactions against sanctions and watchlists and adjudicate hits. Screening runs at onboarding and on list updates across cardholders, clients, and suppliers; a hit blocks processing until dispositioned, and the disposition is retained as evidence.

name: Investigate and file suspicious activity report
description: Investigate an alert and, where warranted, prepare and file the regulatory report. The SAR decision and filing run on the BSA clock from alert qualification; the investigation file must stand on its own for examiner review, and filing is confidential by law.

name: Analyze complaint signal for conduct risk
description: Aggregate and analyze complaint data for unfair or deceptive practice risk. Feeds the UDAAP program: complaint taxonomy, root cause, and trend analysis across channels, including complaints held by servicing clients about serviced portfolios.

name: Set and deploy credit decision strategy
description: Define, test, approve, and deploy changes to the credit decision strategy and its cutoffs. Strategy changes ship through champion-challenger testing with documented approval; the deployed strategy is the single decisioning authority for originations.

name: Develop and validate credit model
description: Build, document, and validate credit and fraud models prior to production deployment. Development evidence, data lineage, and validation results follow model risk management expectations; nothing reaches production without an independent validation record.

name: Execute credit line increase program
description: Identify eligible accounts and execute line increases under the approved strategy. Eligibility, ability-to-pay checks, and notice requirements are built into the program design; execution is batch with opt-out handling.

name: Execute credit line decrease or account action
description: Apply risk-driven line decreases or account actions, with required notice. Adverse action obligations apply to decreases and closures just as they do to declines; the notice must state the principal reasons and bureau information used.

name: Conduct monthly portfolio credit review
description: Review vintage, roll-rate, and segment performance against risk appetite and record the actions agreed at the portfolio credit review.

name: Produce loss forecast and allowance
description: Produce the credit loss forecast and set the allowance for the reporting period. The CECL forecast and allowance feed the financial statements; assumptions, overlays, and approvals are documented for both auditors and examiners.

name: Maintain authorization strategy
description: Define and deploy the rules governing real-time authorization decisions. Authorization strategy balances approval rates, fraud losses, and credit exposure in real time; changes deploy through the same testing discipline as origination strategy.

name: Perform account review and reissue decision
description: Review account risk periodically and decide reissue, close, or continue. Periodic account review drives reissue, line, and closure decisions at card expiry and on risk triggers; decisions carry the same notice obligations as any adverse action.

name: Acquire and refresh credit bureau data
description: Source consumer bureau data for prescreen, account review, and portfolio monitoring under permissible purpose, and manage refresh cadence and quality.

name: Handle cardholder inquiry
description: Receive, understand, and resolve a cardholder inquiry across any servicing channel. First-contact resolution is the design goal across phone, chat, and secure message; anything unresolved routes to a case with ownership and a promise date.

name: Ingest and integrate source data
description: Acquire, integrate, and land source data into the enterprise data platform. Ingestion lands source extracts into the platform with schema validation, lineage capture, and quality checks at the gate rather than downstream.

name: Deploy and monitor production model
description: Deploy an approved model to production and monitor its ongoing performance. Deployment follows model risk approval; monitoring covers drift, stability, and performance against the validation baseline, with retirement triggers agreed up front.

name: Onboard and classify data asset
description: Register a data asset, assign ownership, and classify it for handling. Onboarding assigns owner, steward, classification, and retention up front; the Collibra registration is the system of record this model's stub points at.

name: Measure and remediate data quality
description: Measure data quality against defined expectations and drive remediation. Quality rules run against critical data elements with published thresholds; breaches create remediation work with the data owner, not just a dashboard entry.

name: Publish metadata and lineage to catalog
description: Publish metadata, lineage, and ownership into the governance catalog. The catalog is where consumers discover data and its lineage; publication is part of change delivery, not an afterthought, so the catalog stays current by construction.

name: Execute records retention and disposition
description: Apply the retention schedule and execute defensible disposition of records. Disposition is defensible destruction: eligibility verified against holds, execution evidenced by certificate, and the retention schedule is the single authority.

name: Detect and bucket delinquent account
description: Identify accounts that have missed a payment and assign them to the correct delinquency bucket. Bucketing runs in the nightly cycle and is the trigger for every downstream collections treatment; a bucketing error propagates into contact, reporting, and accounting.

name: Enroll cardholder in digital servicing
description: Register and authenticate a cardholder for web and mobile self-service. Enrollment binds the cardholder to a verified identity with step-up options; weak enrollment is the account-takeover front door, so identity proofing follows the fraud strategy.

name: Serve digital self-service transaction
description: Execute a cardholder self-service action in web or mobile without agent involvement. Self-service actions execute against the same core services as agent actions, with the same entitlements; the channel changes, the control does not.

name: Process cardholder dispute claim
description: Take a cardholder dispute claim, apply provisional credit, investigate, determine, and notify within regulatory timers.

name: Execute network chargeback
description: Submit and track a chargeback through the network within the applicable filing window. Chargeback rights and filing windows differ by network and reason code; a missed window converts a recoverable dispute into an issuer loss.

name: Process representment and pre-arbitration
description: Evaluate merchant representment and pursue pre-arbitration where warranted. Representment evidence is weighed against the reason code requirements; pre-arbitration is pursued only where the economics and the evidence support it.

name: Finalize dispute determination and notify
description: Make the final dispute determination, adjust the account, and issue the compliant notice. The determination closes the Reg E or Reg Z clock: account adjustment, provisional credit disposition, and the written explanation must all land within the window.

name: Maintain target-state architecture and roadmap
description: Define and refresh the target state for each domain and the sequenced roadmap to reach it, aligned to the investment plan.

name: Review solution architecture for an initiative
description: Assess a proposed solution against standards, target state, and risk before funding and again before build; record the decision.

name: Grant or decline an architecture exception
description: Evaluate a request to deviate from a standard, set conditions and expiry, and track the exception to closure.

name: Maintain architecture standards and reference models
description: Author, review, version, and retire the standards and reference models that solution reviews are judged against.

name: Assess technology lifecycle and rationalization
description: Rate each application and platform for tolerate, invest, migrate, or eliminate; identify duplication and end-of-support exposure.

name: Maintain the capability map and process inventory
description: Keep the business architecture model current: harvest changes, run the quality gates, and publish the refreshed model to its consumers.

name: Assess change impact of a proposed system change
description: Trace a proposed system or interface change to the processes, capabilities, and clients it affects, and brief the change authority.

name: Evaluate and select a technology or platform
description: Run the evaluation for a new technology or vendor platform: requirements, options, proof of concept, and a recommendation into procurement.

name: Maintain the application and technology inventory
description: Keep the inventory of applications, platforms, and interfaces complete and attributed, including owner, tier, hosting, and lifecycle state.

name: Recognize interchange and servicing revenue
description: Calculate and recognize interchange, fee, and servicing revenue for the period. Revenue recognition follows the network and client contract terms; interchange, fees, and servicing revenue post to the ledger with support for audit.

name: Process supplier payment
description: Validate, approve, and execute payment to a supplier. Invoices match to contract and receipt before payment; approval limits and segregation of duties are the fraud controls the audit tests.

name: Detect and action transaction fraud alert
description: Detect a suspected fraudulent transaction, action the alert, and contact the cardholder. Alert handling runs against loss and customer-friction budgets; actions span block, reissue, and contact, and the clock matters because exposure grows per transaction.

name: Investigate and adjudicate fraud case
description: Investigate a suspected fraud case and reach a documented determination. The case determination separates true fraud from friendly fraud and abuse, drives the Reg E liability decision, and feeds the loss and strategy data.

name: Respond to account takeover event
description: Contain, remediate, and communicate an account takeover or identity compromise event. Account takeover response contains first, then remediates credentials, reverses fraudulent activity, and communicates with the cardholder; speed limits the loss.

name: Recover and write off fraud loss
description: Pursue recovery of fraud losses and write off the residual with correct accounting. Recovery pursues merchants, networks, and other issuers where rights exist; the residual writes off to the fraud loss line with the accounting evidenced.

name: Submit network fraud reporting
description: Compile and submit fraud reporting to the networks within required thresholds. Network fraud reporting (TC40, SAFE) has thresholds and deadlines; late or wrong reporting risks network compliance programs and fines.

name: Maintain fraud detection strategy
description: Define, test, and deploy changes to fraud detection rules and models. Strategy changes are tested against recent fraud and false-positive performance before deployment; every rule change is versioned and reversible.

name: Manage daily funding position
description: Determine, fund, and report the daily liquidity and funding position. The daily position covers settlement obligations, deposit flows, and contingency lines; a funding miss is a same-day escalation, not a report.

name: Execute monthly financial close
description: Complete the period-end close, including reconciliations, accruals, and reporting sign-off. The close calendar drives reconciliations, accruals, and sign-offs to the reporting deadline; open items age visibly and block sign-off past threshold.

name: Provision and certify access
description: Grant, review, and certify access to systems and data. Access follows least privilege with owner approval; the quarterly certification and automatic revocation of uncertified access are the controls CRI assesses.

name: Detect and respond to security event
description: Detect, investigate, contain, and remediate a security event. Detection through containment runs the incident playbook with severity-driven escalation; the timeline is evidence for both the CRI assessment and any notification duty.

name: Remediate vulnerability
description: Triage and remediate an identified vulnerability within the applicable service level. Severity sets the remediation SLA; breaches escalate rather than languish, and closure requires verification, not just a patch record.

name: Maintain cardholder data scope and evidence
description: Maintain the cardholder data environment scope and the supporting compliance evidence. PCI scope is maintained continuously: network segmentation, asset inventory, and evidence collection, so assessment is a report, not a scramble.

name: Post interchange and settlement entries
description: Calculate and post interchange and settlement accounting entries to the ledger. Interchange entries reconcile to network reports before posting; unexplained variances stop the post rather than flowing into revenue.

name: Build and permission prospect list
description: Source, screen, and permission prospect data for use in acquisition campaigns. Prospect data carries permissible-purpose and suppression obligations; the list that leaves this process is the compliant universe for everything downstream.

name: Construct and approve firm offer of credit
description: Define offer criteria and terms, and obtain compliance approval before release. A firm offer of credit commits the bank under FCRA; criteria, terms, and the compliance sign-off are locked before any channel sees the offer.

name: Execute acquisition campaign
description: Deploy the approved offer across selected channels and manage in-flight performance. In-flight management covers channel performance, budget, and suppression hygiene; changes to a live campaign re-enter compliance review when terms move.

name: Review marketing creative for compliance
description: Review creative, disclosures, and claims for regulatory adequacy before release. Review covers claims, disclosures, and UDAAP risk across every asset and channel; nothing ships without the documented sign-off this process exists to produce.

name: Review campaign performance and adjust targeting
description: Evaluate response, approval, and early vintage economics for in-flight campaigns and decide continue, adjust, or stop.

name: Reconcile network settlement
description: Reconcile network settlement files against internal transaction and ledger positions and resolve breaks.

name: Capture card application
description: Accept and validate a complete card application from any origination channel. Capture is complete when the application has every field decisioning needs and the applicant has the required disclosures; incomplete applications route to cure, not decline.

name: Verify applicant identity and satisfy CIP
description: Verify the applicant's identity and record evidence satisfying customer identification obligations. CIP evidence is retained per BSA requirements; verification failures route to document request rather than automatic decline, and synthetic identity signals feed fraud screening.

name: Screen application for fraud
description: Score and adjudicate the application for synthetic, stolen, and first-party fraud risk. Fraud screening runs before credit decisioning so stolen and synthetic identities never consume a bureau pull; referred applications go to manual review with an SLA.

name: Execute credit decision
description: Apply the approved credit strategy to render an approve, decline, or counter-offer decision with a line assignment.

name: Issue adverse action notice
description: Generate and deliver a compliant adverse action or counter-offer notice within the required period. ECOA and FCRA set the notice content and the clock; the principal reasons must match the actual decision factors, which is exactly what fair-lending testing checks.

name: Establish account and issue credentials
description: Open the account on the core platform and issue the card credential. Account establishment writes the account of record and triggers credential issuance; a failure here strands an approved applicant, which is why it carries a same-day SLA.

name: Manage card production and fulfillment
description: Oversee vendor-executed card personalization, production, and delivery, including inventory, service levels, and exception handling.

name: Provision credential to digital wallet
description: Provision the card credential into a digital wallet or tokenized environment. Wallet provisioning runs the network token flows with step-up verification where risk requires; weak provisioning is a known fraud vector the strategy watches.

name: Handle application withdrawal and abandonment
description: Manage applications withdrawn by the applicant or abandoned before completion. Withdrawn and abandoned applications still carry notice, retention, and bureau obligations; this process closes them compliantly instead of letting them age.

name: Fulfill issuing bank oversight obligations
description: Produce contracted reporting, respond to oversight requests, and manage obligations under the issuing bank agreement.

name: Process authorization request
description: Receive, decision, and respond to a real-time authorization request within the network response window.

name: Ingest clearing file and post transactions
description: Receive network clearing files and post transactions to cardholder accounts. Clearing ingestion matches presentments to authorizations, posts to accounts, and routes exceptions; the file must balance to network totals before posting completes.

name: Process returned payment and assess NSF
description: Handle returned and reversed payments and assess the associated fees. Return handling reverses the payment application, restores the balance, assesses any permitted fee, and feeds NSF patterns to risk; Reg E error claims can start here.

name: Manage token and credential lifecycle
description: Issue, update, suspend, and delete payment tokens and credentials. Token lifecycle events flow between networks, wallets, and the account of record; a stale token strands the cardholder's wallet, so lifecycle sync is monitored.

name: Implement network mandate release
description: Assess and implement network mandate and release changes by the required date. Network mandates carry hard effective dates and fines for misses; assessment, build, and attestation are tracked per mandate from bulletin to production.

name: Fulfill consumer privacy request
description: Receive, verify, and fulfill a consumer privacy rights request within the required period. Identity verification precedes any disclosure; state privacy laws set the clocks and the evidence of fulfillment is retained per request.

name: Design and approve product change
description: Define, price, and obtain approval for a change to a card product. A product change binds pricing, terms, and eligibility; approval spans product, credit, finance, legal, and compliance before configuration starts.

name: Author and version disclosure
description: Author, review, approve, and version cardholder agreements and disclosures. Agreements and disclosures are versioned with effective dates; every account references the version it was disclosed under, which is what makes remediation tractable.

name: Launch product to market
description: Configure, test, and release a product for origination across all affected systems. Launch is a coordinated configuration across origination, core, servicing, and statements, verified in test before the product opens to volume.

name: Retire or migrate product
description: Sunset a product and migrate affected accounts with required notice. Retirement manages the migration and notices for live accounts; terms changes ride the change-in-terms rules, and the product stays resolvable for history.

name: Plan the test strategy for a release
description: Decide scope, risk-based depth, environments, data, and entry and exit criteria for a release before build starts.

name: Build and maintain the automated regression suite
description: Author, review, and prune automated tests so the regression suite stays fast, trusted, and aligned to current behavior.

name: Execute functional and regression testing
description: Run planned functional tests and the regression suite against a candidate build, and record results against the plan.

name: Execute performance and resilience testing
description: Load, soak, and failover-test a candidate against stated capacity and recovery objectives before a material release.

name: Run user acceptance testing with the business
description: Prepare scripts and data, run acceptance with business owners, and obtain their sign-off or documented rejection.

name: Manage defects to closure
description: Triage, prioritize, assign, and verify defects found in test or production, and report defect trends by area.

name: Provision test environments and masked data
description: Stand up and refresh non-production environments with representative, masked data, and retire them on schedule.

name: Certify a release for production
description: Assess test results, open defects, and exit criteria, and issue or withhold the quality certification the change authority relies on.

name: Verify a release in production
description: Run post-deployment checks and smoke tests in production, confirm monitoring is green, and trigger rollback if criteria fail.

name: Place account with collection agency
description: Select, place, and monitor charged-off accounts with an external collection agency. Agency placement follows the approved network with performance and conduct oversight; the agency acts in the bank's name, so its conduct is the bank's risk.

name: Execute debt sale
description: Assemble, price, and execute a sale of charged-off receivables. Debt sale packages carry account-level data quality and documentation warranties; buyer diligence and post-sale complaint routing are part of the process, not after-thoughts.

name: Handle bankruptcy notification
description: Receive, verify, and action a bankruptcy notification with required account treatment. The automatic stay stops collection on notice; verification, claim filing, and account treatment follow bankruptcy chapter rules with dates that are court deadlines.

name: Handle deceased cardholder and estate
description: Verify a deceased notification and manage the account through estate resolution. Estate handling balances recovery with conduct: verified notification stops collection contact, and the claim proceeds through the estate at the estate's pace.

name: Post recovery and account for proceeds
description: Post recoveries and account for proceeds from agency, legal, and sale channels. Proceeds post against charged-off balances with channel attribution; recoveries feed the loss forecast, so mis-posting distorts the allowance.

name: Prepare regulatory reporting data
description: Assemble, validate, and certify the data supporting regulatory reporting submissions. Report data is assembled from governed sources with reconciliation to the ledger and prior submissions; certification is a named officer's sign-off, not a batch job.

name: Accrue rewards earn
description: Calculate and post rewards earn to the rewards ledger for qualifying activity. Earn accrues per the program terms with promotional multipliers; the accrual creates the liability finance reconciles, so earn rules and accounting stay in lockstep.

name: Process rewards redemption
description: Execute a cardholder rewards redemption and settle the resulting obligation. Redemption executes across cash, statement credit, and partner channels; partner settlement follows the program contract, and failed redemptions reverse cleanly.

name: Reconcile rewards liability
description: Reconcile the rewards ledger to the recorded liability and resolve differences. The rewards liability reconciliation catches earn, redemption, and expiry drift between the ledger and finance; differences are investigated, not plugged.

name: Manage issue and remediation to closure
description: Track an identified issue through remediation to evidenced closure. Issues from any source (audit, compliance, self-identified, exam) run one lifecycle: owner, action plan, dates, and evidenced closure that survives challenge.

name: Validate model independently
description: Perform independent validation of a model and record the outcome and conditions. Independent validation is organizationally separate from development; findings condition or block production use, and revalidation triggers are set at approval.

name: Coordinate regulatory examination
description: Coordinate the response to a regulatory examination, including evidence and findings. Exam coordination controls the single flow of requests, evidence, and meetings; every submission is logged and consistent with what other responses have said.

name: Assess interest, fees, and minimum payment
description: Calculate interest, fees, and the minimum payment due for the billing cycle. Cycle assessment applies the cardholder agreement exactly: interest method, fee triggers, and minimum-payment formula, because a systematic error here is a remediation event.

name: Deliver and archive statement
description: Deliver the statement by the cardholder's elected channel and retain it for retrieval. Delivery honors the e-consent election and postal fallback; the archived statement is the legal record retrieved for disputes and subpoenas.

name: Process billing adjustment or goodwill credit
description: Apply approved goodwill credits, fee reversals, and billing corrections. Adjustments carry approval limits and reason codes; patterns feed complaint and conduct analysis because repeated goodwill on the same defect is a signal.

name: Execute account maintenance request
description: Execute a cardholder-requested change to account details or preferences. Maintenance changes execute after authentication with an audit trail; address changes get extra scrutiny because they precede takeover fraud.

name: Authenticate cardholder
description: Authenticate a cardholder to policy before disclosing information or executing a change. Authentication strength scales with request risk; failures route to step-up rather than disclosure, and the policy is tuned with the fraud team.

name: Capture and resolve complaint
description: Capture, classify, resolve, and evidence a cardholder complaint. Complaint handling runs intake through evidenced resolution with regulatory routing where required; the taxonomy feeds UDAAP analysis, so classification is not clerical.

name: Generate and deliver required notice
description: Generate and deliver a regulatory or contractual notice to the cardholder. Notice generation is driven by account events with content owned by legal and compliance; proof of delivery and version are retained per notice.

name: Enroll account in hardship or assistance program
description: Assess eligibility and enroll an account into a hardship or payment assistance program. Hardship enrollment applies documented eligibility consistently; program terms change interest, fees, and reporting, so enrollment is evidenced and reviewed.

name: Maintain servicing knowledge content
description: Author, review, and publish agent-facing knowledge and guidance. Knowledge content is the agent's authority in the moment; review cadence and ownership keep it aligned with policy, because stale guidance becomes wrong answers at scale.

name: Monitor and score servicing interactions
description: Sample, monitor, score, and calibrate servicing interactions for quality and regulatory compliance signal.

name: Administer secured card deposit lifecycle
description: Collect, hold, apply, and refund security deposits for secured card accounts, including graduation and charge-off application, with correct accounting and disclosure treatment.

name: Apply servicemember and military lending protections
description: Identify covered borrowers, apply the required rate and fee protections, and evidence compliance for servicemember accounts.

name: Fund daily network settlement position
description: Determine and fund the daily settlement position with the networks. The settlement position must fund by the network deadline in the settlement currency; a miss is a network compliance event, so the process carries same-day escalation.

name: Reconcile cash and suspense accounts
description: Reconcile cash and suspense account positions and clear aged items. Cash and suspense reconcile daily with aging visible; suspense is a control account, and items that age past threshold escalate to investigation.

name: Investigate and clear settlement exception
description: Investigate settlement breaks and exceptions and drive them to resolution. Settlement exceptions are worked to root cause across network reports, the gateway, and the ledger; recurring breaks feed a fix, not a workaround.

name: Monitor and optimize interchange qualification
description: Monitor interchange qualification rates, identify downgrades, and drive corrections in processing configuration.

name: Cut cycle and generate statement
description: Cut the billing cycle and generate the cardholder statement including the rewards position. Cycle cut is the hard deadline that sequences assessment, statement generation, and delivery; a late cut cascades into payment due dates and regulatory timing.

name: Evaluate and execute portfolio transaction
description: Assess, diligence, price, and execute the acquisition or sale of a card portfolio, through to hand-off into conversion.

name: Deliver software change
description: Design, build, test, and release a software change into production. The umbrella delivery flow from approved demand to production release; the engineering-level decomposition lives in the P-APPDEV and P-QE processes it coordinates.

name: Respond to service incident
description: Detect, triage, resolve, and review a service incident. Incident response runs detect, triage, resolve, and review with severity-driven communication; customer-impacting incidents feed problem management and the resilience picture.

name: Execute disaster recovery test
description: Plan and execute a recovery test against committed recovery objectives. The annual test exercises recovery against committed RTO and RPO with business participation; misses become tracked remediation, and the evidence supports the CRI assessment.

name: Onboard and operate integration
description: Design, register, and operate an interface between systems. Integration onboarding registers the interface, its data, and its owners before traffic flows; unregistered interfaces are how impact analysis goes blind.

name: Configure client program
description: Configure platform, product, treatment, and reporting for a new client program. Program configuration translates the client contract into platform, product, treatment, and reporting settings; every setting traces to a contract clause or a documented default.

name: Convert client portfolio
description: Migrate a client portfolio onto the servicing platform with reconciled balances and no cardholder disruption.

name: Deconvert client portfolio
description: Migrate a client portfolio off the servicing platform and hand over records. Deconversion hands a portfolio off with data, documents, and cutover timing per contract; the obligation to do it well survives the relationship ending.

name: Produce contracted client reporting
description: Produce and deliver reporting to the schedule and specification in the client contract. Contracted reporting ships to specification and schedule; late or wrong reporting is an SLA breach with credits, so production is monitored like any critical batch.

name: Exchange client data feed
description: Send and receive contracted data feeds with the client on schedule. Data feeds run both directions on contracted schedules with schema and quality checks at the boundary; feed failures page, because clients reconcile against them.

name: Bill client servicing fees
description: Calculate and invoice servicing fees per the contract and recognize the revenue. Fee billing calculates from contracted schedules against actual volumes; invoices carry the detail clients audit, and revenue recognition follows the contract.

name: Support client audit or examination
description: Assemble evidence and respond to client and client-regulator oversight requests. Client audits and client-regulator exams get coordinated evidence with the same discipline as the bank's own exams; commitments made in responses are tracked.

name: Intake and deliver client-directed change
description: Receive, price, approve, and deliver a change requested by a servicing client. Client-directed changes are priced, approved, and delivered under the contract's change provisions; scope discipline here is what keeps serviced portfolios profitable.

name: Onboard and diligence supplier
description: Assess, diligence, and contract a new supplier with required security and risk terms. Due diligence is risk-tiered per the TPRM policy; no supplier touches cardholder data before security review and contract terms land, which is the EX.DD control.

name: Monitor supplier risk and performance
description: Monitor supplier risk, performance, and service levels through the relationship. Ongoing monitoring covers risk, performance, and financial condition on a tier-driven cadence; findings route to the relationship owner with dates.

name: Execute supplier exit
description: Execute the exit of a supplier, including data return and service transition. Exit executes the termination plan: service transition, data return or destruction with certificate, and access revocation, proving the exit clause was real.
